anchor.quote: Add images only if they help the user

not_rules.note: Section heading grouping general guidance on image usage (G-1).

anchor.quote: You must get permission (a licence) to use copyright material. This includes images and text.

not_rules.note: Legal/administrative compliance advice for writers, not an automatable text rule (G-5).

anchor.quote: Read the government copyright rules in the Australian Government intellectual property manual.

not_rules.note: Process guidance directing author to another manual (G-5).

anchor.quote: Choose diverse images that are clear and simple

not_rules.note: Section heading (G-1).

anchor.quote: Choose images that reflect and support the diversity of Australia’s peoples and cultures, especially if you are using images of people.

not_rules.note: Editorial/curatorial advice regarding graphic asset selection (G-5).

anchor.quote: Use the same font and typeface, line thickness and colour scheme in all images of the same type.

not_rules.note: Graphic design instruction concerning asset production rather than text editing.

anchor.quote: Include decorative images only if they are relevant to the content

not_rules.note: High-level editorial principle (G-5).

anchor.quote: Don’t use images to fill in space. Decorative images must still be relevant. Use images that relate directly to the content.

not_rules.note: Editorial guidance on content curation (G-5).

anchor.quote: Use alt text, captions and titles to explain images

not_rules.note: Section heading grouping child rules on alt text and captions (G-1).

anchor.quote: Set the correct resolution and file type

not_rules.note: Section heading for asset compression and technical file settings (G-1, not_text).

anchor.quote: Don’t embed images with a large file size into content that you will publish online, such as PDFs or webpages. Optimise and compress all image files so they make it quicker for the user to access the information.

not_rules.note: Technical file-size optimization rule for assets (not_text).

anchor.quote: Design for mobile devices first. An image will scale to the device people view it on. Check that it’s easy to read on a mobile phone screen and a desktop.

not_rules.note: Web design and testing advice (G-5).

anchor.quote: There are many file types for images. Seek specialist advice to optimise an image file as a vector or raster file format.

not_rules.note: Advice directing user to seek technical specialist advice (G-5).

anchor.quote: Use graphs, charts and maps if they explain complex information

not_rules.note: Section heading (G-1).

anchor.quote: Use graphs, charts and maps for information that is too detailed for the text. Don’t use them if another format meets the user need – such as a list, table or tool.

not_rules.note: Content format selection advice (G-5).

anchor.quote: Don’t add borders or background tints.

not_rules.note: Graphic design instruction for visual chart styling (not_text).

anchor.quote: Use gridlines only where they help people read the data.

not_rules.note: Graphic design instruction for chart formatting (not_text).

anchor.quote: Use ‘tick marks’ on the x- and y-axes to show the scale of data intervals at a glance. Avoid more than 10 tick marks on the y-axis.

not_rules.note: Visual chart design guideline (not_text).

anchor.quote: Add legends and units of measurement to complex images

not_rules.note: Section heading grouping specific visual requirements (G-1).

anchor.quote: All graphs, charts and maps should have a legend that tells people the meaning of lines, colours and symbols.

not_rules.note: Visual composition specification for image assets (not_text).

anchor.quote: Refer to informational images in the text

not_rules.note: Section heading grouping rules on referencing images (G-1).

anchor.quote: Place the image close to where you mention it in the text. For example, a graph must be on the same page and after the paragraph that refers to it.

not_rules.note: Layout/typesetting advice for writers/designers (G-5).

anchor.quote: You don’t need to refer to decorative images and illustrations in the text unless they are part of the discussion.

not_rules.note: Permission relaxing the requirement to reference images (G-3).

anchor.quote: Check any details that feature in both the text and an image. For example, the text might quote numbers from a graph. It is easy to make a last-minute change to one and forget to correct the other.

not_rules.note: Advice to the writer to double check consistency (G-5).

rules.quote: Add alt text to all images.
rules.violation_condition: an image element without an alt text attribute or description
rules.why: Clear instruction governing document markup for images; G-1, G-2.

rules.quote: Include captions for all images that are not decorative.
rules.violation_condition: a non-decorative image lacking a caption
when: Images that are decorative do not require a caption.
rules.why: Direct instruction on image captions with explicit exception for decorative images; G-2.

rules.quote: Use real text rather than images of text whenever technically possible.
rules.violation_condition: an image containing text where real text could be used
rules.why: Accessibility rule against rasterized text; G-2, G-3.

covers.quote: Don’t use colour as the only source of meaning. Try adding dots and dashes to lines and cross hatching to areas.

rules.quote: Make sure that colour is not the only visual means of conveying information in graphs and diagrams.
rules.violation_condition: a graph or diagram where colour is the sole method used to distinguish or convey data
rules.why: Consolidates identical WCAG requirement stated under Accessibility requirements and chart guidelines; G-4.

rules.quote: Maps must also have a scale bar and an arrow to show which way is north.
rules.violation_condition: a map lacking a scale bar or a north arrow
rules.why: Unambiguous normative requirement for map elements.

parts.quote: Figure 6 shows an example of good ergonomic posture.

examples.note: Repeats caption / descriptive text and uses sensory direction

parts.quote: The photograph of an ideal workstation set-up (see left) shows an example of good ergonomic posture.

rules.quote: Don’t repeat the whole caption of the image in the text. Instead, use a locator number to refer to it, for example ‘Figure 1’.
rules.violation_condition: in-text reference that repeats the entire image caption rather than citing a locator number (e.g. 'Figure 1')
rules.why: Direct style instruction paired with explicit Like this/Not this examples.

rules.quote: Don’t refer to ‘the photograph on the left’. This sensory language is not accessible for some users.
rules.violation_condition: spatial or sensory positional references (such as 'on the left', 'above', 'below') used to identify an image in the text
rules.why: Specific rule prohibiting sensory/spatial directional language for accessibility.

examples.note: Interprets trend rather than repeating exact figures

parts.quote: European Union expenditure more than quadrupled from 2016 to 2018 (Figure 7).

examples.note: Merely repeats raw data from the figure

parts.quote: Figure 7 shows European Union expenditure increased from US$9 million in 2016 to about US$40 million in 2018.

rules.quote: Ensure your text comments on or interprets the image, rather than repeating the text or data in it.
rules.violation_condition: text accompanying an image that merely repeats the data or text from the image rather than commenting on or interpreting it
rules.why: Direct rule accompanied by explicit compliant and violating examples.

rules.quote: Avoid referring to a page number in the text because page numbers can change during the publishing process.
rules.violation_condition: mentioning a specific page number in the body text when referring to an image or figure
rules.why: Clear textual negative constraint.

covers.quote: notes to superscript locators (such as a superscript ‘#’, ‘a’ or ‘1’)
source of data (use the appropriate form for author–date or documentary–note).

rules.quote: List notes in the following order:
rules.specification: Order must strictly be: 1. abbreviations, 2. notes to superscript locators, 3. general note to the image, 4. source of data.
rules.violation_condition: image notes listed out of the specified sequence (abbreviations; notes to superscript locators; general note; source of data)
when: Applies when notes appear below an image.
rules.why: Prescribes precise ordering of image note components; G-1, E-3.

rules.quote: Don’t include this information in the caption or in ordinary footnotes or endnotes.
rules.violation_condition: image note information (abbreviations, locators, general image note, or data source) placed inside the caption or in ordinary document footnotes/endnotes instead of below the image
rules.why: Prohibition on placing image note information into captions or body footnotes.

rules.violation_condition: image notes that are not left-aligned
rules.why: Explicit layout instruction for image notes.
